If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with upward momentum bias.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward drift.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and true price exceeds forecast by >1.5%, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture lagged momentum.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon to reflect overbought sentiment correction.

If sentiment is consistently 0.00 over 5+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to account for delayed market reaction.

If forecast consistently underestimates true price by >1.0% over 3+ consecutive days, apply +0.5% correction to next forecast regardless of sentiment to avoid persistent bias.
